Malignancy-associated hypercalcemia is a neoplastic/paraneoplastic syndrome
Sarcoidosis is a multisystem inflammatory syndrome

assignments.reason: Dysphagia is a symptom related to gastrointestinal disorders, making B2 the most taxonomically compatible parent.
Gastroesophageal reflux disease is a direct exemplar of the B2 parent, making it the most appropriate choice.
Hyperparathyroidism is an endocrine disorder, and B4 is the parent that best represents this classification.
Malignancy-associated hypercalcemia is more closely related to neoplastic/paraneoplastic syndromes, making B3 the most appropriate parent.
Sarcoidosis is a multisystem inflammatory syndrome, and while it could fit under other categories, B5 is the most specific and appropriate parent.
Tuberculosis is primarily a respiratory infection/inflammation, making B1 the most taxonomically compatible parent.
Vitamin D toxicity is related to endocrine disorders, specifically those involving calcium and phosphorus metabolism, making B4 the most appropriate parent.
Vomiting is a symptom rather than a disease, and thus does not fit well under any of the provided parents without more context.
